title: Entry edit and delete live in a Preview-topped drawer with tap-to-expand rows only
context: Decision 0136 gave summary rows both a left-swipe reveal and tap-to-expand. Both showed the same actions, so the swipe added a second, non-exclusive way to open a row without adding anything, and the developer chose to remove it.
decision: Summary leaves the Options dialog and becomes a bottom drawer whose top edge is the Preview. Idle, it shows only the handle and the latest entry (the former Preview); opening it lifts the latest entry with the edge so that it becomes the list's first row in place. Summary therefore leaves the panel, and its gestures no longer compete with the panel's. Tapping a row is the only way to show its actions: it expands inline (an accordion), one row at a time, to show recordedBy, the time and the full actions, keeping the context in the list; rows have no swipe gesture. The buttons follow the last-entry rule: the latest entry offers edit and delete (the request carries the version number and shares the guard of sync-recording's D9 and D10), any other offers edit and roll back to here, so the alternative path is visible instead of a disabled delete. Gestures split with the input Preview: idle, a tap opens the drawer; during input, a tap on the Preview only submits (three steps complete submits, otherwise nothing happens); the handle always toggles the drawer. Opening the drawer by its handle during input lifts the draft, pulsing, into the list's first row, clearly apart from committed entries; once submitted and frozen it becomes the real first entry in place.

alternatives.option: Version A: tap shows the same action buttons as the swipe
alternatives.reason: The least UI and no extra layer, but it cannot reveal recordedBy and other information.

alternatives.option: Version C: tap opens an action sheet
alternatives.reason: Rows keep their shape, but another layer stacks on the drawer and the context leaves the list.

alternatives.option: A permanent kebab button per row, or a long-press menu
alternatives.reason: Entry rows have no horizontal room left and per-row buttons are visual noise; long press has no visible affordance, against the principle that unavailable is not invisible.

alternatives.option: A disabled delete button with explain-on-tap for entries other than the last
alternatives.reason: Replaced in place by a roll-back-to-here button: the alternative path is visible and usable, better than learning it is unavailable only after a tap.

alternatives.option: Keep the left-swipe reveal alongside tap-to-expand
alternatives.reason: It showed the same actions as tapping, could leave one row swiped open while another was expanded, and duplicated a gesture the panel already uses; a native rewrite can reconsider gestures.
